subject: Trajectory demo recap — eval artifacts & model-delta mitigation
messages:
From: Maria Delgado <maria@trinity.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@trinity.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — follow-up + sample prompt set

Hi Olga,

Really appreciate the demo today — it helped the team see the text-generation flow end-to-end. A few quick asks so we can move to a scoped eval: 

- Can you send the prompt set we discussed (we'll run a 10k-sample smoke test)?
- Any recommendations for 1-2 model variants to try for intent extraction + short-form generation at 512 tokens?
- Do you have lightweight benchmark artifacts we can point engineering at?

We're sensitive about output drift — we recently had a vendor push a minor model update that slightly shifted label distribution on our intents, so acceptance criteria will include regression checks. I'll attach a short acceptance criteria doc.

Thanks,
Maria Delgado
Head of ML Integrations
Trinity AI

Attachment: trinity_acceptance_criteria.docx

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Maria Delgado <maria@trinity.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up + sample prompt set

Maria — great to meet you and the engineering leads. Recap below plus the artifacts we promised.

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: intent extraction + concise generation for email-summary and follow-up copy at ~512 tokens; 95%+ intent accuracy target and low hallucination for entity fields.
- Constraints: throughput target 20 req/s with p95 < 220ms; initial eval will run on a 10k prompt sample you provided.

Recommended model variants for evaluation (first-pass):
1) redwood/align-medium-v2 (balanced latency/cost; good on extraction)
2) redwood/optimize-small-quant (lower-cost option; watch edge-case hallucination)

Artifacts attached:
- trinity_prompt_set_v1.json (the cleaned prompt set we discussed)
- redwood_benchmarks_trinity.pdf (runbook + throughput/latency profiles on dedicated vs hosted)
- diff_report_20261121.csv (example diff script output format we use to flag regressions)

Guidance on regression checks:
- Run exact-match + macro-F1 on intent labels pre/post model swap.
- Produce a small 'diff report' (we attached a sample) that lists prompt id, old_output, new_output, token-delta, and a simple severity tag (info/warn/blocker).
- If severity >= blocker on >0.5% of core intents, request pin/rollback.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You run smoke 1k locally from the attached prompt set and share raw outputs.
2) Redwood provides an eval runner and a per-prompt diff script (see attached sample) — we can run on hosted or on your dedicated trial slot.
3) If you observe actionable regression, we will: canary traffic to the previous pinned variant, or execute an emergency pin (we can support both).

I'll leave detailed rollback/pinning ops to Aditya and Marissa — cc'ing them so we can scope SLA/commitments for TR-4819.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: trinity_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_benchmarks_trinity.pdf, diff_report_20261121.csv

From: Maria Delgado <maria@trinity.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@trinity.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up + sample prompt set

Thanks Olga — receiving the artifacts now. A few clarifications from our side after a quick smoke run: 

- The small-quant variant showed a handful of hallucinated entities on our 'payment method' slot (~0.3% of 1k), which is borderline but concerning since finance downstream is strict.
- Our infra lead asked about clear SLAs for rollback latency — if we detect a regression in production, can Redwood pin to a prior variant within 15 minutes and provide the diff report with severity tags?
- Also: we'd like the eval runner to produce both token-cost estimates and a per-prompt severity ranking so our PM can triage.

Procurement is looping in the security checklist next week; happy to coordinate a short call to confirm the rollback SLA and access controls.

-Maria

Quoted: "If severity >= blocker on >0.5% of core intents, request pin/rollback." — from Olga's note

Attachment: trinity_acceptance_criteria.docx (resubmitted)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Maria Delgado <maria@trinity.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up + sample prompt set

Looping in ops plan and quick commitment for TR-4819.

Operational commitments (we can sign these as part of the Dedicated POC addendum):
- Emergency pin window: we can pin to the last validated variant within 10 minutes of a signed request from the account's primary admin (we will need a signed access control form from Procurement).
- Canary rollout tooling: We will run a canary at 5% (configurable) for 30 minutes and produce the diff_report.csv with severity tags. If blocker severity exceeds 0.5% across core intent set, automate rollback to pinned variant.
- Access & audit: every pin/rollback will generate an audit event and a snapshot of the debug KV cache for forensic replay.

Immediate next steps for us (action items):
1) Olga: share the eval runner credentials with Maria and a short README for running on hosted eval slot.
2) Marissa: prepare a one-page addendum (POC rollback SLA + admin auth template) and share by EOD Mon.
3) Aditya/Infra: prepare a small playbook for the canary -> auto-rollback path (we'll include runbooks for pin vs rollback and the expected time-to-recover).

I'll also attach a short template we give customers for the admin auth (I'll DM the signed form process to Procurement).

—Aditya Rao
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0102
